error_codes.auth_unavailable: Authentication is temporarily unavailable, for example when every password hashing slot is busy; try again shortly.
error_codes.bad_request: The request is malformed, such as a body that isn't valid JSON.
error_codes.conflict: The request conflicts with the current state, when no more specific code applies.
error_codes.cross_origin_request_denied: A cookie-authenticated, state-changing request came from an origin that isn't allowed (cross-site request forgery protection).
error_codes.email_not_verified: The account's email address must be verified first: to sign in, or to create organisations and send invitations.
error_codes.error: Any other 4xx status without its own code.
error_codes.forbidden: The caller is signed in but lacks the permission: a platform role for `/ops`, an organisation role for org-scoped endpoints, or, for an API key, a scope.
error_codes.internal_error: An unexpected error. The detail never includes the cause; it is logged once with the request ID.
error_codes.invalid_job_config: The job configuration is outside the allowed bounds, such as a schedule more often than once a minute or a timeout that isn't a duration.
error_codes.invalid_setting_value: The value isn't valid JSON, or fails the setting's type or constraints.
error_codes.maintenance: Maintenance mode is on (`maintenance.enabled`). The detail is `maintenance.message`; `Retry-After` is `maintenance.retry_after`.
error_codes.message_required: The example echo endpoint got a blank message.
error_codes.method_not_allowed: The path exists but not with this HTTP method.
error_codes.mfa_required: The permission needs a session signed in with a second factor: turn on two-factor authentication and sign in again.
error_codes.not_found: No route matches the method and path, or a resource wasn't found and no more specific code applies.
error_codes.session_required: The operation needs the person's signed-in session, not an API key: managing the account, sessions, API keys and service accounts, and joining or leaving organisations.
error_codes.rate_limited: Too many requests from this client or for this operation; wait for `Retry-After`.
error_codes.request_too_large: The request body is larger than `APP_MAX_BODY_BYTES`.
error_codes.too_many_attempts: Too many sign-in, code, second-factor or re-authentication attempts within the window; the detail says when to try again.
error_codes.unauthenticated: The endpoint needs a signed-in session (cookie or bearer token).
error_codes.unauthorized: Authentication failed, when no more specific code applies.
error_codes.unavailable: The service or a dependency is temporarily unavailable.
error_codes.validation_failed: The request doesn't match the operation's schema, or a resource's fields aren't valid. `errors` lists each field.
error_codes.weak_password: The password doesn't meet the password policy; the detail says why.
error_codes.account_banned: An operator banned the account; it can't sign in until the ban is lifted (ADR-0070).
error_codes.storage_off: The app has no file storage configured: set STORAGE_DRIVER (ADR-0075).
error_codes.invalid_storage_key: Keys are 1 to 1024 characters of path segments without ".", ".." or a leading slash.
error_codes.storage_unavailable: The storage service didn't answer: check the endpoint, bucket and keys.
error_codes.preview_not_found: No email preview has this name; `GET /_dev/mail/previews` lists them (ADR-0074).
error_codes.invalid_address: The recipient isn't an email address.
error_codes.impersonation_off: Impersonation exists only while the app runs with the dev console (`orb dev`), never in production (ADR-0070).
error_codes.user_not_found: No account has this ID; deleted accounts are gone to operators too.
error_codes.rate_limiter_not_found: The app has no rate limiter with this name, or the key was empty (ADR-0070).

error_code_where.account_banned: Every sign-in: password, second factor, passkey, Google, Apple, GitHub, and impersonation.

audit_actions.auth.account.deleted: A user deleted their account (`DELETE /v1/auth/me`). The account is kept for `auth.deleted_account_retention`, then purged.
audit_actions.auth.accounts.purged: The `auth_cleanup` job removed accounts deleted longer ago than `auth.deleted_account_retention`.
audit_actions.auth.accounts.unverified_expired: The `auth_cleanup` job deleted accounts whose email address was never verified within `auth.unverified_account_ttl`.
audit_actions.auth.email.verified: A user verified their email address with the emailed code.
audit_actions.auth.identity.apple_notification: Apple sent a server-to-server notification about a linked Apple account, such as consent revoked or the account deleted.
audit_actions.auth.identity.linked: A Google, Apple or GitHub account was linked: at sign-up through the provider, or by a signed-in user (`flow`: `id_token`, or `web` for a link through the provider's page).
audit_actions.auth.identity.revocation_abandoned: The `auth_revoke_tokens` job gave up revoking a provider's tokens after its attempts.
audit_actions.auth.identity.unlinked: A user unlinked a Google, Apple or GitHub account.
audit_actions.auth.keys.rotated: `rotate-auth-keys` re-encrypted two-factor secrets with the first `AUTH_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` key.
audit_actions.auth.login.failed: A sign-in failed: wrong password, unknown account, unverified provider email, invalid passkey and so on. `reason` says which.
audit_actions.auth.login.succeeded: A user signed in and a session was created.
audit_actions.auth.mfa.challenge_failed: A second factor at sign-in was wrong, used or expired.
audit_actions.auth.mfa.challenge_succeeded: A user passed the second-factor step of sign-in.
audit_actions.auth.mfa.recovery_code_used: A recovery code was used as the second factor; the user is emailed.
audit_actions.auth.mfa.recovery_codes_regenerated: A user replaced their recovery codes.
audit_actions.auth.mfa.reset: An operator turned off a user's two-factor authentication with `reset-mfa`.
audit_actions.auth.mfa.totp_disabled: A user turned off authenticator app two-factor authentication.
audit_actions.auth.mfa.totp_enabled: A user confirmed authenticator app setup; two-factor authentication is on.
audit_actions.auth.mfa.totp_enrollment_started: A user started authenticator app setup.
audit_actions.auth.passkey.clone_warning: A passkey's signature counter didn't increase, which suggests a cloned authenticator; the ceremony was refused.
audit_actions.auth.password.changed: A signed-in user changed their password.
audit_actions.auth.password.reset: A user set a new password with a reset code; their sessions end.
audit_actions.auth.password.reset_requested: A password reset code was requested for an existing account.
audit_actions.auth.reauth.failed: A signed-in user's password or second factor was wrong when confirming a sensitive change.
audit_actions.auth.role.granted: An operator gave a user a platform role with `grant-role`.
audit_actions.auth.role.revoked: An operator took a platform role away with `revoke-role`.
audit_actions.auth.session.revoked: One session ended: logout, or the user revoked it from their session list.
audit_actions.auth.user.created: An operator or seed data created an account (`CreateUser`), not through sign-up.
audit_actions.auth.user.registered: Someone signed up, with a password or through Google, Apple or GitHub.
audit_actions.flags.flag.changed: An operator changed a feature flag's state through `PUT /ops/flags/{key}`, with a reason. The metadata summarises the new state (enabled, default, percentage, how many organisations and users are targeted); the IDs themselves are in the flag's history.
audit_actions.flags.flag.reset: An operator reset a feature flag to the state declared in code through `DELETE /ops/flags/{key}`, with a reason.
audit_actions.jobs.definition.changed: An operator changed or reset a job's configuration through `/ops/jobs/definitions/{name}`.
audit_actions.jobs.definition.run_requested: An operator ran a job now through `/ops/jobs/definitions/{name}/run`.
audit_actions.jobs.run.cancelled: An operator cancelled a job run.
audit_actions.jobs.run.retried: An operator retried a job run.
audit_actions.auth.api_key.created: A user created a personal API key, or an operator or organisation admin created a key for a service account. Records the key's ID, owner and scopes, never the key.
audit_actions.auth.api_key.expired: The `auth_cleanup` job found API keys past their expiry. Records the count.
audit_actions.auth.api_key.revoked: An API key was revoked: by its owner, by an operator or organisation admin, or because its user reset their password, deleted their account or its service account was disabled.
audit_actions.auth.service_account.created: An operator (platform) or organisation owner or admin (organisation) created a service account.
audit_actions.auth.service_account.deleted: A service account was deleted; its keys stop working.
audit_actions.auth.service_account.disabled: A service account was disabled; its keys are revoked permanently.
audit_actions.auth.service_account.updated: A service account's name, description or roles changed.
audit_actions.mail.suppression.added: A signed Resend webhook reported a hard bounce or complaint, and the address was added to the suppression list. The event records the reason and suppression ID, never the address.
audit_actions.mail.suppression.removed: An operator removed an address from the suppression list through `DELETE /ops/mail/suppressions/{id}`, with a reason.
audit_actions.mail.test.requested: An operator sent a test email through `POST /ops/mail/test`.
audit_actions.ops.incident.opened: An operator opened an incident (`POST /ops/incidents`), or the `incidents_detect` job opened an automatic one because the server error rate crossed `incidents.error_rate_threshold`. Metadata holds the source, status and severity, never the title.
audit_actions.ops.incident.updated: An operator added a timeline update to an incident (`POST /ops/incidents/{id}/updates`), or `incidents_detect` noted that an automatic incident's error rate recovered or rose again. Metadata holds the status, severity and update kind, never the message.
audit_actions.orgs.invitation.accepted: An invited person accepted an invitation.
audit_actions.orgs.invitation.created: A member invited someone to the organisation.
audit_actions.orgs.invitation.resent: A member resent an invitation, with a new link.
audit_actions.orgs.member.added: Someone joined the organisation, by accepting an invitation.
audit_actions.orgs.member.removed: A member was removed, by another member or because their account was deleted.
audit_actions.orgs.org.created: An organisation was created, including each user's personal workspace (`personal`).
audit_actions.orgs.org.deleted: An organisation was deleted; it can be restored until `purge_after`.
audit_actions.orgs.org.purged: The `orgs_purge` job removed an organisation deleted longer ago than `orgs.deleted_org_retention`, with its data.
audit_actions.projects.project.created: A project was created. The example resource: resources made with `orb gen resource` record the same three actions.
audit_actions.projects.project.updated: A project was changed; `fields` lists which.
audit_actions.retention.purged: The `retention` job deleted data older than its retention setting, one event per kind of data.
audit_actions.settings.value.changed: An operator changed or reset a runtime setting through `/ops/settings/{key}`; `reason` is required for security-relevant settings.
audit_actions.auth.email.verified_by_operator: An operator marked the address verified (ADR-0070).
audit_actions.auth.user.banned: An operator banned the account; metadata holds the reason. Its sessions and API keys were revoked (ADR-0070).
audit_actions.auth.user.deleted_by_operator: An operator deleted the account: what the owner's own deletion does, without their password (ADR-0070).
audit_actions.auth.session.revoked_by_operator: An operator ended one session (metadata `session_id`) or every session (`sessions`) of the account (ADR-0070).
audit_actions.auth.passkey.removed_by_operator: An operator removed a passkey from the account (ADR-0070).
audit_actions.auth.identity.removed_by_operator: An operator unlinked a Google, Apple or GitHub account (ADR-0070).
audit_actions.auth.user.impersonated: An operator started a session as the user, in development only; metadata holds `session_id` and `mfa_verified` (ADR-0070).
audit_actions.storage.object.uploaded: An operator uploaded an object through /ops/storage; the resource is the key (ADR-0075).
audit_actions.storage.object.deleted: An operator deleted an object through /ops/storage (ADR-0075).
audit_actions.storage.object.moved: An operator moved an object; the resource is the new key, `from` the old one (ADR-0075).
audit_actions.storage.directory.created: An operator created a directory marker (ADR-0075).
audit_actions.storage.signed_url.created: An operator created a signed download or upload link; the metadata says which and until when (ADR-0075).
audit_actions.ops.rate_limit.reset: An operator forgot a key's rate-limit budget; the resource is the limiter's name, never the key (ADR-0070).

jobs.gorbital.mail.send: Delivers queued email through the configured provider: up to 8 attempts of 30 seconds each on the `default` queue, and a message the provider rejects is cancelled instead of retried. The app enqueues one for every email it sends; it has no schedule and isn't a job definition, so `/ops/jobs/definitions` doesn't list it, but its runs appear in `/ops/jobs/runs`.
